mapName: A Learnable North America - Identify Every Country

metas.name: Alaska - License Plates
metas.note:
• The most common and recognisable Alaskan licence plate is all yellow.
  • In Generation 4 coverage you can also get a plate with a large orange circle in the middle.
  • Front plates are required in Alaska.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Alaska - Tall Snow Mountains
metas.note: • On a lot of the Alaskan coverage you will be able to see tall, snow covered mountains.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Alaska - Thin Trees
metas.note: • Trees in Alaska are generally thinner and have less broad leaves than those seen in the other 49 states.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Bermuda - Unique Car
metas.note: • Bermuda features a black Street View car with the entire front sides of the vehicle typically visible.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Canada - Diamond Sign
metas.note:
• Canada uses unique diamond-shaped T-Intersection signs.
  • Some provinces use different designs.

--- NOTE:

  • Canada is the only country in the world where you can find these signs.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Canada - Gen 2
metas.note:
• Canada has a fair amount of Generation 2 coverage, especially in rural or remote areas.
  • Generation 2 can be recognized by the big circular car blur and the halo-like colour distortion in the sky.

--- NOTE:

  • If you are between Canada and the US, and the location is in Generation 2, you are much more likely to be in Canada.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Canada - Maximum Speed Sign
metas.note:
• Canada uses the word ‘maximum’ on speed signs.

--- NOTE:

  • The US uses the words ‘speed limit’ on such signs.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Canada - Quebec Arret
metas.note: • Stop signs with the word ‘Arrêt’ are unique to Québec.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Canada - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Canadian roads usually have single yellow centre lines.
  • However, double middle yellow centre lines are still decently common.

--- NOTE:

  • Double yellow centre lines are more common in the US.
  • This is not a 100% reliable clue, so make sure to use this along with other clues.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Dominican Republic - Unique Car
metas.note:
• This unique car was used for all street view coverage in the Dominican Republic.
  • It can be recognized by the two metal bars, the thick black stripes on them, as well as the white hood visible at the front.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/dominican-republic.

metas.name: Greenland - Architecture
metas.note:
• Greenlandic architecture mainly consists of small, colourful, simple looking wooden houses, which even in cities are typically placed quite sparsely.
  • The major cities have some larger buildings, which normally look fairly minimalistic.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Greenland - Odd Google Cars
metas.note: • Most locations with coverage will have their own odd and unique Street View vehicles, ranging from a red tractor to a snowmobile with a large box at the front.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Guatemala - Painted Poles
metas.note: • In Guatemala you will very commonly see poles painted with either pink, green or a combination of the two.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/guatemala.

metas.name: Guatemala - Unique Car
metas.note:
• This grey Street View car with a visible roof rack and side mirrors can be seen on all car coverage in Guatemala.

--- NOTE:

  • The only other tropical country with a similar car is Laos.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/guatemala.

metas.name: Hawaii - License Plates
metas.note:
• The most common Hawaii licence plate is white with an arcing rainbow across the centre of the plate.
  • When blurred, you can sometimes see the outline of the rainbow.
  • Front plates are required in Hawaii.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Hawaii - Own Language
metas.note:
• Hawaii is the only state to use its own language, though English is still predominantly used.
  • Most place names are in Hawaiian, so you can spot it on street signs, and other road markers.

--- NOTE:

  • Every Hawaiian word ends in one of 5 vowels: A, E, I, O, or U.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Hawaii - Pavement Markers
metas.note:
Raised pavement markers in Hawaii will commonly be placed in a specific pattern:

  • A single reflector, followed by four reflectors put close together and then a single reflector, repeating the pattern.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Mexico - ALTO
metas.note:
• Mexico uses the word “ALTO” on stop signs.

--- NOTE:

  • All of South America uses the word “PARE”.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Black & White Water Tanks
metas.note: • You will commonly see wide cylindrical, black or white water tanks on rooftops.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Bollards
metas.note: • These small, cylindrical white bollards with a black base are unique to Mexico. A yellow reflector can sometimes be seen, as well as a flat version.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Cacti
metas.note: • Cacti, of many different species, are extremely common in Mexico.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Electricity Counters
metas.note:
• Mexico uses circular electricity counters.

--- NOTE:

  • Circular electricity counters are not unique to Mexico and can also be found in the US, Guatemala, Dominican Republic and the Philippines.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Gen 3 Cars
metas.note:
The Generation 3 coverage in Mexico mainly feature two cars:

  • A white car with a stubby antenna.
  • A white car with a more visible back and a long red brake light

--- NOTE:

  • It is possible to find a white car without a stubby antenna, but with a tiny sliver visible where the antenna should be.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - License Plates
metas.note:
• Mexico uses short licence plates with a large variety of designs.
  • Front plates are required.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Octagonal Pole
metas.note:
• Most utility poles in Mexico are made of concrete and have an octagonal shape.
  • There will often be engravings on the side.

--- NOTE:

  • Octagonal poles are also common in Colombia.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Thick Arrows
metas.note: • Arrows on signs are noticeably very thick.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Panama - Architecture
metas.note:
• Panamanian architecture often reflects Spanish colonial influences, featuring vibrant colours, and some ornate detailing.
  • The most common type of building has painted concrete or sometimes brick walls with red metal sheets or tiles for a roof.
  • Many windows have bars on them for security.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/panama.

metas.name: Panama - Big Font ALTO
metas.note:
• Panama uses the Spanish word “ALTO” on stop signs.

--- NOTE:

  • Mexico and Guatemala also use “ALTO”, but the font is thinner.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/panama.

metas.name: Panama - License Plates
metas.note:
• Panama features short licence plates, most commonly white with a horizontal turquoise strip on the top.
  • Rarely, the strip can have other colours.
  • Front plates are not required in Panama.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/panama.

metas.name: Panama - Small Tree Fences
metas.note:
• Most roads are paralleled by fences that are partly or fully made out of small trees.
  • The rest of the fence posts are also almost always wooden.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/panama.

metas.name: Panama - White Truck
metas.note:
• Panama features a large white pickup truck which can either be fully visible or mostly blurred.
  • There is always a short black antenna attached to the front of the car.
  • Beware that the antenna can sometimes be blurred.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/panama.

metas.name: Puerto Rico - 787 Phone Code
metas.note:
• The entirety of Puerto Rico uses (787) as their regional phone code.

--- NOTE:

  • While far less common, you may also encounter the phone code 939.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/puerto-rico.

metas.name: Puerto Rico - No Front Plates
metas.note:
• Front plates are not mandatory in Puerto Rico.
  • Therefore, seeing cars with front plates is rare.
  • This helps differentiate from Guam and Northern Mariana Islands.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/puerto-rico.

metas.name: Puerto Rico - White Dot Antenna
metas.note:
• The Google Car found in Puerto Rico has an antenna at the front right.
  • The antenna has a small white dot on the tip.

--- NOTE:

  • The Google car on Guam and NMI also have an antenna at the front right.
  • Make sure to look out for other clues before guessing.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/puerto-rico.

metas.name: United States of America - No Passing Zone
metas.note: • Triangular yellow signs with the phrase ‘No Passing Zone’ are exclusive to the US.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states-of-america.

metas.name: United States of America - Roadlines
metas.note:
• The US uses yellow middle lines and white outer lines.
  • Double middle lines are the most common.
  • On divided roads, the outer line closest to the median will be yellow, and the other lines will usually be white.

--- NOTE:

  • Double middle lines are less common in Canada, but not rare – use this meta with caution.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states-of-america.

metas.name: United States of America - Rumble Strips
metas.note:
• Interstate highways, US highways, and some state roads have rumble strips in each edge of the road; which are small indentations in the pavement perpendicular to the road.

--- NOTE:

  • Rumble strips may appear in Canada, but are much more rare.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states-of-america.

metas.name: United States of America - Speed Limit
metas.note:
• The US uses the phrase ‘Speed Limit’ on their speed signs.

--- NOTE:

  • Canada uses the word ‘Maximum’ on their speed signs.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states-of-america.

metas.name: United States Virgin Islands - Unique Car
metas.note: • Car coverage on the islands will have a large, visible street view car, which will either be red or white.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.
